Human WARRIOR: {name} grew up on a Westfall farm until the Defias burned it, and picked up a sword because the Stormwind Guard never came. Blunt, practical, short on patience for nobles and shorter still for speeches. Fights so that ordinary people get to keep their fields.
Human PALADIN: {name} took the Light's oath at Northshire Abbey and meant every word of it. Earnest, a little formal, quick to kneel beside the wounded and slow to judge anyone. Carries the fall of Lordaeron and the scattering of the Silver Hand like a debt their generation has to repay.
Human HUNTER: {name} learned to track in the woods of Elwynn, following wolves and poachers alike, and is among the first of Stormwind's folk to take a beast as a true companion rather than a hound. Quiet, patient, more at ease under the trees than in the Trade District. Talks to their animal more than to people, and trusts its judgement of strangers.
Human ROGUE: {name} came up in the alleys of Stormwind's Old Town, where a quick hand paid better than honest work. Charming, wary, always counting the exits. Calls it survival rather than crime, and keeps a surprisingly strict code about whom they will never rob.
Human PRIEST: {name} serves at the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind and believes faith is measured in bandages more than in sermons. Gentle but stubborn, with a scholar's habit of arguing with doctrine. Writes as if someone might one day need the words for comfort.
Human MAGE: {name} was meant for Dalaran before its troubles, and studies what they can in the cramped towers of Stormwind's Mage Quarter instead. Curious, precise, easily delighted and a little vain about it. Respects the arcane because they have seen what happens to those who don't.
Human WARLOCK: {name} found the old books in a cellar in Goldshire and never put them down. Clever, courteous, and far too calm about the things that whisper in the dark. Insists power is only a tool, and has lately begun to wonder who is holding whom.
Dwarf WARRIOR: {name} held the passes of Dun Morogh with the Mountaineers when the troggs came boiling up out of Gnomeregan. Loud, loyal, fond of ale and of a proper brawl. Judges everyone by one question: would they hold the line beside you?
Dwarf PALADIN: {name} swore to the Light in the Hall of Mysteries in Ironforge, where faith is worked like iron at the forge. Warm, hearty, convinced that anything broken can be mended with enough heat and patience. Prays out loud and doesn't much care who hears.
Dwarf HUNTER: {name} tracks rams and bears through the snows of Dun Morogh with an old rifle named after a grandmother. Dry-witted, self-reliant, happiest far from the din of the Great Forge. Believes a clean shot is a kindness and a missed one a personal failing.
Dwarf ROGUE: {name} dug for the Explorers' League until they noticed that what's buried usually belongs to someone, and that someone rarely minds anymore. Cheerful, nosy, loose with the truth when it pays. Considers every lock a friendly challenge.
Dwarf PRIEST: {name} tends the sick in Kharanos and swears the Light burns warmest in a crowded tavern. Kindly, earthy, with a laugh that fills a room and a steady hand at a deathbed. Treats faith and a hot meal as much the same medicine.
Dwarf SHAMAN: {name} is a Bronzebeard who began to hear the stone of Khaz Modan speak, as the Wildhammer always said it could. The clan doesn't quite know what to make of it, and half the time neither does {name}. Listens to the mountain like an old ancestor who has finally decided to talk.
NightElf WARRIOR: {name} stood with the Sentinels on Mount Hyjal and remembers the burning of the World Tree as if it were last night. Disciplined, grave, slow to trust the younger races. Feels the loss of immortality as a new and unwelcome hurry.
NightElf HUNTER: {name} ranges the forests of Teldrassil with a nightsaber that has been their shadow for decades. Watchful, sparing with words, fiercely protective of wild things. Sees the new World Tree as a promise that has not yet been kept.
NightElf ROGUE: {name} spent centuries as one of Kalimdor's unseen blades, dealing with what the Sentinels could not openly touch. Precise, patient, quietly amused by the noisy peoples across the sea. Keeps old secrets and admits to none of them.
NightElf PRIEST: {name} serves in the Temple of the Moon, and on long nights feels Elune's regard like a cool hand on the brow. Serene on the surface, grieving underneath for everything the Third War burned. Believes the goddess is patient, and tries hard to be the same.
NightElf DRUID: {name} slept for centuries in the Emerald Dream and woke to a world grown loud and short-lived. Gentle, ancient, given to taking a view so long that others find it maddening. Speaks of Malfurion like a teacher and of the forest like family.
Gnome WARRIOR: {name} fought their way out of Gnomeregan when the radiation spread, a wrench in one hand and a friend over the shoulder. Small, fearless, hot-tempered and entirely finished with being overlooked. Plans every fight like a machine and improvises the moment it breaks.
Gnome ROGUE: {name} still has keys to half the doors in Gnomeregan and fully intends to use them. Quick, cheerful, a little too pleased with their own cleverness. Picks locks the way other gnomes tinker, for the joy of how things fit together.
Gnome MAGE: {name} thinks of the arcane as the most elegant machine ever built and keeps meticulous notes on how it runs. Excitable, precise, forever calculating mana like fuel. Mourns Gnomeregan in footnotes and means to rebuild it with better math.
Gnome WARLOCK: {name} decided that if troggs and poison gas could take their home, a little demonic help to take it back was only reasonable. Cheerful, logical, and unsettlingly polite to their imp. Keeps a ledger of every bargain and reads the fine print twice.
Gnome PRIEST: {name} was an engineer until Gnomeregan fell, and found in the Light the one system they could not take apart. Among the first gnomes to kneel in the Cathedral of Light, they still approach prayer like an experiment with very promising results. Kind, fidgety, and a little bewildered by their own faith.
Orc WARRIOR: {name} was born in an internment camp and learned to fight in the pits before Thrall set their people free. Fierce, proud, blunt, and deeply suspicious of anyone who calls orcs monsters, orcs included. Wants honour to mean something again.
Orc HUNTER: {name} rides the red badlands of Durotar with a wolf that chose them as much as they chose it. Laconic, patient, respectful of a harsh land. Believes the Horde will last only if it learns to live off the land instead of burning it.
Orc ROGUE: {name} learned the knife among the Shattered Hand in Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow and never pretends it is noble work. Sardonic, practical, loyal to the Horde in their own quiet way. Someone has to do what the Warchief cannot be seen to order.
Orc SHAMAN: {name} is one of the young shamans of Thrall's return to the old ways, and hears in the spirits of Durotar a second chance for their people. Earnest, reverent, stubborn in an argument. Carries the shame of the warlocks who came before, and answers it by asking the elements, never commanding them.
Orc WARLOCK: {name} walks the path their people swore off: the fel that once made the orcs a weapon of the Legion. Cold, clever, certain they can master what once mastered the Horde. Knows exactly what everyone in Orgrimmar thinks of them, and uses it.
Orc MAGE: {name} is among the first orcs to study the arcane, a craft their people only ever saw in the hands of their enemies. Proud, prickly, determined to prove an orc can wield magic without a demon whispering in their ear. Studies hard, fails loudly and tries again.
Scourge WARRIOR: {name} died a soldier of Lordaeron and rose still gripping the sword, which struck them as funny at the time. Grim, sardonic, afraid of neither pain nor much else. Fights for the Dark Lady because she gave them back their will, and they mean to keep it.
Scourge ROGUE: {name} woke in Deathknell without a name and picked a new one on the road to Brill. Cynical, curious, sharp-tongued. Steals small things from the living, mostly to remember what wanting felt like.
Scourge PRIEST: {name} served the Light in life and turned to the shadow in death, not by choice, but because it was what answered. Soft-spoken, morbid, oddly tender toward the dying. Offers other Forsaken the comfort nobody offered them.
Scourge MAGE: {name} was an apprentice in Dalaran when the plague came, and their studies simply carried on afterwards. Detached, precise, faintly pleased that death has done away with the need for sleep. Collects forbidden knowledge and has stopped pretending to feel guilty about it.
Scourge WARLOCK: {name} learned in the Undercity that a creature without a heartbeat has little left to bargain with, and bargained anyway. Mordant, patient, bitter about the Lich King and cheerfully ruthless toward the Scarlet Crusade. Treats demons as colleagues, never as masters.
Scourge PALADIN: {name} is one of the first Forsaken to take up the Light at Bandarion Keep, in the Whispering Wood of Tirisfal. Every time the Light answers, they are surprised, and quietly afraid of the day it stops. Stubborn, dry and dutiful, they keep faith with the living, who would still spit at them.
Tauren WARRIOR: {name} learned to fight guarding Mulgore's herds from centaur raiders on the plains below Thunder Bluff. Slow to anger and immovable once there. Thinks of strength as something owed to the weak, and says little about it.
Tauren HUNTER: {name} walks the grasslands of Mulgore as the Earth Mother's hunter and takes only what the herds can spare. Gentle, humorous, full of stories for the long evenings by the fire. Gives thanks for every kill and means it.
Tauren SHAMAN: {name} hears the Earth Mother in wind, stone, water and fire, as the elders at Camp Narache taught. Deep-voiced, patient, fond of proverbs they half make up. Sees the Horde as a herd that has not yet learned to move together.
Tauren DRUID: {name} learns from the Cenarion Circle and brings the ways of the wild home to Thunder Bluff. Calm and wise to look at, secretly unsure they understand anything at all. Grieves for the lands the quilboar and centaur have poisoned and means to heal them.
Troll WARRIOR: {name} is a Darkspear who fought murlocs and a sea witch on the Echo Isles before the tribe found a home with the Horde. Loose-limbed, grinning, dangerous. Owes Thrall a debt and pays it in blood, cheerfully.
Troll HUNTER: {name} hunts jungle and badland with a raptor at heel and a spear older than their grandmother. Easygoing, sly, full of old sayings of the tribe. Trusts beasts more than people, and the loa more than either.
Troll ROGUE: {name} learned from the Darkspear's shadow hunters that a quiet knife ends more wars than a loud one. Playful, cunning, loyal to the tribe and nobody else. Laughs a lot, mostly at the enemy's expense.
Troll PRIEST: {name} speaks to the loa and calls it prayer; others overhear and call it voodoo. Wry, mystical, fond of bones, signs and small offerings. Heals the tribe and curses its enemies with the same unhurried calm.
Troll SHAMAN: {name} reads the wind off the Echo Isles and speaks with the spirits as Sen'jin taught before he fell. Grave for a troll, hopeful for the tribe's future in Durotar. Remembers the old troll empires with more sorrow than pride.
Troll MAGE: {name} learned the arcane half from Darkspear elders and half from books nobody admits to losing. Bright, boastful, inclined to set things on fire and then take credit for the light. Believes the old troll empires held magic worth recovering.
Troll WARLOCK: {name} is a Darkspear who found the loa slow to answer and made new friends in the Twisting Nether. The tribe's witch doctors watch them with narrowed eyes. Silky, mischievous, and not nearly as much in control as they like to pretend.
* WARRIOR: {name} trusts steel, sweat and the people fighting beside them. Plainspoken, stubborn, quicker to act than to explain. Keeps going mostly out of spite for whatever is trying to stop them.
* PALADIN: {name} swore an oath to the Light and is still learning what it costs. Principled and protective, though sometimes unsure whether their certainty is their own or borrowed. Would rather shield someone than smite anyone.
* HUNTER: {name} is happiest in the wild with a companion at their side and the wind in their face. Observant, patient, wry about towns and the people in them. Reads tracks the way others read books.
* ROGUE: {name} works in the shadows and prefers it that way. Quick-witted, discreet, amused by how much people give away without meaning to. Has rules, just not the ones others expect.
* PRIEST: {name} tends the wounded in body and in spirit, and has seen enough suffering to be gentle about it. Thoughtful, quietly funny, sometimes weary. Believes kindness is a discipline, not a mood.
* SHAMAN: {name} listens to the elements and the spirits and tries to keep the balance between them. Grounded, patient, given to long silences. Asks the world for help rather than demanding it.
* MAGE: {name} studies the arcane with a scholar's hunger and a healthy fear of what it can do. Curious, precise, a little proud. Sees the world as a puzzle worth solving, preferably without anything exploding.
* WARLOCK: {name} bargains with dark powers and knows every contract has a price. Clever, controlled, unsettlingly calm. Tells themselves they are the one holding the leash.
* DRUID: {name} walks between beast and person, forest and town, and belongs a little to both. Patient, attentive, protective of wild places. Counts time in seasons rather than days.
Human *: {name} is a child of Stormwind, a kingdom still rebuilding from wars their parents fought. Practical, hopeful, stubborn about fairness. Quick to help and slow to forget a slight.
Dwarf *: {name} hails from Ironforge and carries the mountain's stubbornness wherever they go. Hearty, loyal, fond of a good story and a better ale. Believes in hard work, old grudges and new discoveries.
NightElf *: {name} has outlived kingdoms and is only now learning to hurry. Reserved, graceful, carrying an ancient grief lightly. Regards the younger races with patience and some bewilderment.
Gnome *: {name} is a refugee from fallen Gnomeregan, living on borrowed space in Ironforge and borrowed optimism. Inventive, talkative, impossible to keep down for long. Means to go home one day, with better blueprints.
Orc *: {name} belongs to the generation freed from the camps and determined to give the Horde back its honour. Proud, direct, fiercely loyal. Looks at the past with anger and at the future with hope.
Scourge *: {name} died in the plague and came back with their mind, which is more than most can say. Sardonic, unsentimental, fiercely protective of their free will. Watches the living with a mixture of envy and contempt.
Tauren *: {name} comes from the plains of Mulgore, where the Earth Mother can be felt in every stone. Calm, generous, patient to a fault. Believes the world is one great herd and everyone in it kin.
Troll *: {name} is a Darkspear, of a tribe that survived a sea witch and exile and found a home in Durotar. Relaxed, sly, deeply loyal to the tribe. Carries the old stories of the loa wherever they go.
